card.title: Tradition Outranks Explanation
card.instruction: Treat inherited customs as meaningful because they have been repeated. Preserve each step and resist every request to explain why it still matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we launch the boat, three circuits. Grandad always started at the bow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why three? The tide's right now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He did three every launch. Come round to the bow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already walked round twice carrying the ropes. Can those count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with ropes. Grandad collected those afterwards. Put them back and we'll begin properly.

mechanism: A repeats Grandad's circuits and rope order as their own justification, refusing to count similar practical work as completion.
confusable: Unlike adding new ceremony whenever one ends, A protects the exact inherited sequence because it has repeatedly been done that way.
comparison: The launch alternative insists on the original rope-free circuits; the bowl alternative insists the honored bowl remain empty.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
